title: How to use spark connect with Kubernetes cluster
question:
I'm currently trying to setup spark connect on kubernetes. I'm just wondering if anyone has done this. I'm trying to figure out if I need to setup a stand alone spark cluster on kubernetes for the spark connect service using my own helm chart or if I can use the kubernetes master as the spark master for spark connect service and it will handle the creation of the executors for the cluster.

I have tried running spark connect locally with my own stand alone cluster and it works correctly, but I can't figure out how to configure spark connect with kubernetes. Can I use the kubernetes master URI?

If I try doing ./pyspark --remote "sc://kubernetes-master" the shell launches, but just hangs if I try to read data and nothing is happening on the kubernetes cluster in terms of pods being generated.
answer:
I stumbled on this as well. It's actually straightforward.

You have to start the server like this (source):

bin/spark-submit --class org.apache.spark.sql.connect.SimpleSparkConnectService

If you want to use it on Kubernetes (leveraging Spark-Submit) you'll have to start it like this:

${SPARK_HOME}/bin/spark-submit \
    --master k8s://$KUBERNETES_SERVER \
    --deploy-mode cluster \
... ADDITIONAL spark config ... \
    --conf spark.kubernetes.container.image=$IMAGE \
    --class org.apache.spark.sql.connect.SimpleSparkConnectService \
    local:///opt/spark/jars/spark-connect_2.12-3.5.0.jar

Just make sure that you pass spark-connect_2.12-$SPARK_VERSION.jar as target jar to the cluster. I put it into the image since I don't want to create unnecessary downloads on the maven repositores.

If you want to use connect, you'll have to do a port-forward to your local machine.

kubectl port-forward NAME_OF_THE_DRIVER 15002

From that point on you can use pyspark --remote 'sc://localhost'.
